    #671. Breaking: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (785 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
    • A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
    • According to recent reports, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

    A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

    According to recent reports, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

    In a recent development, the broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

    Industry observers note that the Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

    According to the investigators, Akbay is stated to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

    According to recent reports, it is not new for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

    In a recent development, sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

    Sources indicate that in the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

    Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

    Esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen states Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

    Esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he notes, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

    According to recent reports, several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    In a recent development, the Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and declared its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, highlighted how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

    It has been revealed that "These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

    #670. Want to see your live AI usage on your Mac’s icons? This clever new app lets you

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (776 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

    Want to see your live AI usage on your Mac’s icons? This clever new app lets you

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that there’s a new way to keep an eye on your AI usage and when your limits reset: by using your Mac’s app icons.
    • Sources indicate that designer Michael Flarup has just launched a upcoming Mac utility called IconSwapper, which lets you replace any app’s official icon with one of your own creation.
    • Doing so is fairly simple, and you don’t have to be technically minded to get this to work.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that there’s a new way to keep an eye on your AI usage and when your limits reset: by using your Mac’s app icons. Yes, really!

    Sources indicate that designer Michael Flarup has just launched a upcoming Mac utility called IconSwapper, which lets you replace any app’s official icon with one of your own creation. While you can use this tool to change your icons’ appearance, design, shading, and more, one of the more interesting ways to use it is to swap the icons for AI apps like ChatGPT or Claude with versions that can display your live AI usage.

    Doing so is fairly simple, and you don’t have to be technically minded to get this to work. After installing the app on your Mac, you simply choose which application you want to create a “live” icon for — meaning one that responds to a particular app.

    Besides tracking AI usage in ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, you can also create live icons for a number of the built-in Mac apps like Messages, Mail, Safari, Finder, Music, and others like Chrome and Spotify, but these configurations tend to be more fun than they are practical. For instance, you can configure Safari’s compass to follow things like page loads and downloads, or you can make it so that the Finder guy’s eyes follow your cursor around the screen. (That one is hilarious!).

    Of course, there are plenty of other ways to track your AI usage — you don’t need an icon to do that. You can track usage from your account or your harness, even from a fun little gadget. But tracking it from the icon adds a certain whimsy to your Mac desktop setup. (If your dock is crowded, note that you can also see your icon customizations from your tab bar as you switch apps.).

    Beyond live icons, you can also change what an icon looks like using IconSwapper’s built-in tools.

    There are a surprising number of built-in customizations that are as easy to use as clicking a few buttons or toggling a switch. IconSwapper also comes with a large library of alternative icons for every app that are already ready to use, or you can upload your own.

    Industry observers note that flarup is based in Copenhagen, where he runs a design studio, and he has been drawn to icon design and customization for years. He’s been making his own Mac icons since the early 2000s and even wrote a book about app icons that celebrates the work of designers.

    He had been working on a solution that would allow him to customize Mac icons, which had proven tricky because macOS has no official support for theming and protects its system icons. To work around this, he came up with a different technique that involves drawing directly on the icons without replacing them, allowing him to use shaders, motion, and display real data.

    Flarup tells TechCrunch that his renderer runs the icon artwork through custom Metal shaders in real time.

    “The breakthrough was figuring out how to send the Dock a bitmap for another running app and have it draw that frame itself,” he explained. “I spent a lot of time getting the artwork to follow the icon through all the little ways macOS moves it, from Dock magnification to the Command-Tab switcher. Once I had that working, I could make the icon react to whatever’s happening,” Flarup mentioned.

    That lets people configure icons to do all kinds of fun, new things they never could before, like make light move across a gold icon as you drag your cursor over it, or animate an app’s icon while it’s thinking.

    “That opens up a lot of fun ways to make your Mac feel like yours. I’ve always felt the software we use every day could be a little more fun and a lot more personal,” he added.

    The app itself is a one-time purchase of $19 as a launch promo but will later sell for $29, its website states.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner.
    • The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the massive powers.
    • Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner.

    The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the massive powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

    Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

    Despite countries not being required to reveal how they voted, it is thought Grynspan’s candidature has been resisted by Russia and the US, two of the five permanent security council members that can ultimately wield a veto against a candidate. Knowledge among the security council delegations of how countries are voting is down to private intelligence, leaks and a process of elimination.

    The intensive lobbying over the job has spread across the globe, but Friday is especially notable since the poll is slated to differentiate the voting of the P5 from the 10 elected members (E10) of the security council. To be recommended as secretary general to the UN general assembly, a candidate needs nine votes and no vetoes. In Friday’s colour-coded secret ballot, the P5 will cast red ballots and the E10 white.

    One diplomat stated: “The electoral system means it is notable how many votes you win, but equally how many of certain votes you don’t lose.”.

    The protracted 140-day deadlock confirms the polarisation that has hampered the incumbent secretary general, António Guterres, but also belies claims the role is now an irrelevance.

    Friday’s secret ballot may also reveal whether the United Arab Emirates’ campaign for its diplomat, Lana Nusseibeh, is about to blow up in its face due to the hostility to the UAE’s brand of active, commercially driven diplomacy, not just in Sudan, but also Somalia, Western Sahara, Libya and Yemen.

    It has been revealed that A late entrant, in the two straw polls in which she has contested so far, Nusseibeh secured only seven “encourage” votes, six “discourage” and two “no opinions”. This is despite prestigious massive-power backing and her acknowledged personal diplomatic skills.

    Nusseibeh has US and Russian backing. The French foreign ministry may have misgivings about the UAE, but Emmanuel Macron, the French president, travelled to the UAE in the midst of French riots to see the UAE president, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and secure 100,000 metric tons of diesel a month.

    In the UK, the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has kept his counsel, but he shares a Polish-Jewish refugee heritage with Grynspan and cannot be an admirer of the UAE’s human rights record or its evasion of EU sanctions on Russia. The prime minister, Andy Burnham, has UAE connections from his time as mayor of Manchester, and Nusseibeh is a fellow alumnus of the University of Cambridge. At the UN she worked closely with the UK in an informal group called “Friends of the Future of the UN”.

    Yet 68 British MPs, including the Labour chair of the international development select committee, Sarah Champion, last week signed a letter calling on Burnham to veto Nusseibeh, describing her as “a tainted and compromised figure”.

    It has been revealed that some of the opposition to her from elected security council members is not wholly political. Latin American countries believe an informal rotation system means it is their turn to lead the UN. As a result Panama and Colombia, at the moment on the security council, will oppose her. China has also been supportive of this rotation principle.

    Sources indicate that but others deeply object to what they consider to be the UAE’s dollar diplomacy and preparedness to use its extraordinary wealth to exacerbate and exploit pre-existing divisions in a country to gain a commercial foothold. Somalia, for instance, has a seat on the Security Council, and its president, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, this week went on TV to accuse the UAE of buying ports, establishing military bases and supporting armed forces outside Somalia’s national security framework without federal approval.

    Recent findings suggest that it is also possible that Finland and Latvia, the two elected members with the greatest stake in Ukraine, are unimpressed that the UAE gave Vladimir Putin red carpet treatment when he visited Abu Dhabi in December 2023, nine months after the international criminal court had issued an arrest warrant for child trafficking. Greece, less engaged in Ukraine, may be more flexible.

    Industry observers note that since the last poll, Nusseibeh has been to Bahrain, Britain and Pakistan, a clue as to where extra votes may be harvested. She also had a “thoughtful exchange” with Zeng Jixin, the Chinese ambassador to the UAE.

    The two hurdles are whether someone so deep inside the UAE inner circle would have the courage in office to show true independence, and whether her active denials of UAE involvement in arming the RSF in Sudan leave her irretrievably tainted. From a Palestinian intellectual family, she insists she would make peace in Sudan her number one priority.

    It has been revealed that in the last ballot on 5 November, Grynspan won 12 votes in favour and three negative. But on 16 October – the only colour-coded ballot so far – which distinguishes between permanent and elected members – she received two discourage votes from permanent members, the equivalent of a veto. Nusseibeh had not joined the race at that point.

    In an administration as personalised as the US, it has been hard for Grynspan to gain influence, with many sensing that Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, is the key influencer.

    Grynspan has been reluctant to make the fact she is Jewish a feature of her candidacy, but the election of a Jewish person to run the UN might be seen as something the US could embrace as transformative. Her age – she is 70 – could be considered a drawback among those calling for a younger generation to renew the institution.

    In a recent development, although there are other Latin American candidates, Grynspan is seen as a more viable candidate than her rival, the Argentine Rafael Grossi, the head of the UN weapons inspectorate. Russia has opposed Grossi, objecting to his interventions over the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant in Ukraine.

    One way or the other, the logjam has to be broken soon.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Watch: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold?
    • Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (Â£1.34 trillion).
    • The artificial intelligence (AI) tech giant's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold?

    Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (Â£1.34 trillion).

    The artificial intelligence (AI) tech giant's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.

    Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 each, showing there was plenty of excitement around AI.

    Yet the manufacturer, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it?

    In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.53, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day as the shares closed at $97.17.

    Some investors stated Anthropic's debut seemed to be a success, as shares rose roughly 17% during the day, but the broader tech market did not perform as well.

    Recent findings suggest that the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index closed down nearly 2.3%. Stocks fell in the largest tech firms, including Google's parent manufacturer Alphabet, which was down by 2.9%, while Amazon lost almost 3.9%.

    The buildout happening around this era of AI is among the most expensive endeavours in the history of technology, with more than $1 trillion being spent in the last year alone by a handful of major tech companies.

    The speed at which investment has grown has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble.

    "Bubbles don't burst on the day of the largest deal," Richard Whittle, an economist with the University of Salford remarked. "They burst later, if the positive future becomes suspect.".

    Anthropic has made one of the fastest trips from start up to IPO in history.

    While the basics of the technology have been around for decades, the more recent advent of more powerful computers and related components have allowed the processing of more data than ever.

    The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet more swiftly.

    It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.

    As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.

    The "initial exuberance" will wear off, Barringer stated, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.

    That organization, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.

    Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.

    Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.

    But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.

    With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially massive future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.

    "There's no obvious peer to compare it to," Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, mentioned.

    Simon Jack: Can Anthropic's record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?

    Daniela Amodei: Anthropic and the price of AI.

    So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth more than $1.7 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.

    "We'll have a stab at it," Wilson mentioned. "I don't think anyone really knows.".

    A few things will likely impact the firm's success on the stock market in the near-term.

    One of those things is the prospect of fresh laws governing the use of AI tools. In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already stated they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.

    Industry observers note that such regulation is presently unlikely at the federal level. US President Donald Trump on Thursday spoke about AI during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, alongside Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

    Trump reiterated his position against "any form of robust regulation" around the technology, adding, "we won't allow that to happen, frankly.".

    The same day, however, a bipartisan group of US lawmakers formed the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, which will work specifically on AI regulation and safety considerations.

    A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself. Firm executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.

    Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI organization that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.

    Daniela Amodei, Anthropic's president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company "had an AI safety team before we launched our first product".

    "AI carries real risks," she added.

    Despite the company's claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.

    Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut.

    Tech Report: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1201 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.
    • Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.
    • Industry observers note that if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.

    Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.

    Industry observers note that if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

    “We’ve got this,” Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company’s third quarter earnings call.

    Recent findings suggest that by Thursday, the tech giant’s stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia’s biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected.

    Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period last year up to total $115.8 billion, driven by data center revenue that was up 110 percent and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the highly anticipated Vera Rubin platform, which shipped during the quarter, becoming the “fastest product ramp in firm history,” Kress told investors.

    It has been revealed that “Our momentum is real,” Kress stated. “With the market-leading multiyear roadmap, supply agreements extending through to the end of the decade, and sustainable demand, we are well positioned to accelerate Nvidia’s leadership position.”.

    But investors are stilltrying to reconcile Nvidia’s stellar recent financial performance and position as a central pillar in the AI economy with serious concerns over its future.

    The organization’s stock has taken a stunning tumble in recent weeks. Fueled first by a broader market sell-off of chip stocks amid concerns about the AI bubble, the stock took another blow following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, according to US intelligence sources cited by The Newly introduced York Times.

    In a recent development, harvey Jones, Nvidia’s newly appointed chairman of the board, told investors on the call Tuesday that the firm “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and has already tapped an executive search firm to help find a replacement. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company ever since — famously without a succession strategy — has become essentially inseparable from it in the eyes of Wall Street and the media. But while Huang may not be ready to let go, posting on X this week that he’d be “honored” to be reinstated as CEO, Nvidia’s executive suite seems ready to move on.

    It has been a tumultuous two and a half weeks for Nvidia.

    On October 29th, The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Jensen Huang to be the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The report centered on his “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center organization and one of Nvidia’s clients. Nvidia initially contested the report, adding that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang “are not unusual or unexpected.”.

    Industry observers note that nvidia’s stock seemingly remained unaffected by the reports, at least at first. The share price closed at $213.66 on October 29th, down just 0.8 percent from the previous day. (Julian Barnes, one of the reporters on the story, later commented, “I will confess I was kind of surprised that the world’s initial reaction to our October story was a bit muted.”) The stock closed at a 4 percent drop the next day as the entire Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent, the worst single-day decline since June.

    According to recent reports, the stock continued to fall through Wednesday, November 4th, the day after the blue wave swept the midterms, stoking fears on Wall Street that the fresh class of Democratic governors in key states like Texas would slow down data center construction. On Thursday, November 5th, Nvidia’s stock fell 9.2 percent, its largest single-day drop in at least a year. But chip stocks began to recover the next day, and by close on Friday, November 6th, Nvidia was back up 2.8 percent to a share price of $186.64.

    It has been revealed that then all hell broke loose. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang sent a tech giant-wide memo to Nvidia staff in which he apologized for engaging in an extramarital affair. The memo coincided with the opening of an independent investigation by Nvidia’s board into Huang’s alleged misconduct and whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. Huang said he would cooperate fully with the investigation. By the opening bell on Monday, November 9th, Nvidia shares had tumbled 7 percent and trading volume surged past its three-month average as investors reacted to the memo. After a brief rebound, the stock continued to oscillate the next day, as more details of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang’s relationship emerged. By the time the market closed on Tuesday, November 10th, Nvidia shares were down to $168.89, nearly 10 percent below the closing price on the last day of 2025.

    The stock rebounded slightly on Wednesday, November 11th, as investors prepared for Nvidia’s third quarter earnings call, scheduled for the following Tuesday, November 17th. By Wednesday night, however, shares had plunged yet again as media reports circulated that Nvidia’s board was considering ousting Huang, and other reports emerged detailing a second alleged affair, this time between Huang and an Nvidia employee.

    Nvidia announced Huang’s departure on the morning of Thursday, November 12th, sending the manufacturer’s shares falling nearly 14 percent at the open. It closed at just a 4.3 percent dip. The intraday low of $148.80 per share was its lowest price in a year.

    Sources indicate that on December 1st, Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews. Nvidia’s general counsel will do the same on December 2nd.

    In a recent development, retail investors have already seized the opportunity to buy the dip. In the first 30 minutes of trading on Thursday, November 12th, retail investors bought $111 million of Nvidia shares in the largest-ever first half-hour of opening for the stock, Bloomberg reported, citing Vanda Research.

    Nvidia’s average price target is $232.59, with the lowest estimate at $130 and the highest at $350, according to an analysis of analyst projections over the last three months by Google Finance.

    Nearly two-thirds of those analysts issued a “Buy” rating for Nvidia in the last three months. Of those, all 30 reiterated that rating post-earnings.

    The stock closed at $145.98 on Thursday, a latest 52-week low.

    Then again, numbers are the core basis for stock market ratings, and numbers may not be Nvidia’s problem right now. It’s everything else — the leadership vacuum, upcoming congressional testimony, regulatory uncertainty, broader questions about neocloud customer financing and sales to China — that will continue to impact the stock in the coming weeks.

    Elon Musk notes SpaceX has a proposal to eliminate cell phone dead zones

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CEO Elon Musk noted SpaceX has completed the design of a miniature rooftop cell tower that could provide better coverage to mobile phones and eliminate dead zones inside buildings where signals from its Starlink satellites have trouble reaching.
    • These mini cell towers are expected to go into production in 2027, Musk noted, during an interview at the DealBook Summit this week.
    • “We’ve got a strategy that enables ubiquitous access on Earth, including via cell phone,” Musk noted, noting the company is launching its Direct-to-Cell V2 satellite constellation next year, which will increase bandwidth 40-fold.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CEO Elon Musk noted SpaceX has completed the design of a miniature rooftop cell tower that could provide better coverage to mobile phones and eliminate dead zones inside buildings where signals from its Starlink satellites have trouble reaching.

    These mini cell towers are expected to go into production in 2027, Musk noted, during an interview at the DealBook Summit this week.

    “We’ve got a strategy that enables ubiquitous access on Earth, including via cell phone,” Musk noted, noting the company is launching its Direct-to-Cell V2 satellite constellation next year, which will increase bandwidth 40-fold. “But there is a missing piece of the puzzle here which is that if you’re indoors, especially if you have a metal roof, that blocks the signal from space. So we need something that’s terrestrial that addresses situations where people are, you know, in a building with a thick roof essentially.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the firm’s efforts initially focused on buying wireless spectrum after receiving the Federal Communications Commission’s approval in 2024 to move forward with intends to offer a direct-to-phone version of its Starlink satellite internet service, in partnership with T-Mobile. SpaceX struck a $17 billion deal with EchoStar in 2025 and agreed this year to acquire a portfolio of low-band spectrum valued at $8 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that combining that wireless spectrum with mini cell towers should boost signals and end the dead zone problem, he said. According to Musk, the organization has completed the design of what he described as “a micro cell tower thing that you just put on your roof, like a Starlink dish.”.

    Musk, who has a history of missing his own production deadlines, demurred, saying the devices were “going into production, I think, next year.”.

    The idea isn’t new, but it wasn’t clear until this week how much progress SpaceX had made toward developing the hardware.

    SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell noted during the organization’s August earnings call that it wouldn’t use massive cell towers and would instead deploy small, low-power cellular base stations.

    In a recent development, even with this latest progress report, SpaceX appears to be still working out the details. Musk mentioned one approach would be to bundle the small cellular base stations together with Starlink terminals.

    SpaceX’s plan to build a hybrid cellular-satellite network has fueled speculation, and even predictions, that legacy telecom companies could be in danger. But Musk doesn’t think so, because he expects an entirely new class of customers to drive demand for wireless bandwidth: AI.

    “I don’t think this means, like you know, AT&T, Verizon, or others go out of business or anything,” he mentioned, adding that maybe they’ll lose some revenue. “But I actually think that the demand for bandwidth will be tremendous in the future, and a lot, and that bandwidth will be driven primarily by superintelligence and robots, and they’re going to need a lot more bandwidth than humans.”.

    EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.
    • This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.
    • During the delegations' meeting, Burnham remarked the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

    This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

    During the delegations' meeting, Burnham remarked the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

    Recent findings suggest that "This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham said.

    Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa remarked the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

    He mentioned jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

    Burnham said that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

    He went further and remarked "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up newly introduced opportunities" for young people.

    Von der Leyen said the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

    She said the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

    Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

    She also said Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

    Burnham remarked the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

    In September, Burnham stated he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

    "Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.

    The three key agreements establish ways to:.

    The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

    According to recent reports, no deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

    "There will be further discussions coming out of it on challenges including on tuition fees," Burnham said.

    Von der Leyen ‌stated ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

    In a recent development, on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

    They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

    According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

    Leaders mentioned they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

    The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

    On Monday, Burnham stated it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

    Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

    Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed noted Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.
